title: Cannabis Pot Roast with an Infused BBQ Glaze
h1: Not Your Average Pot Roast: Smoked and Finished with an Infused Glaze
metaDescription: Smoke or oven-braise a chuck roast, then finish each plate with a measured cannabis BBQ glaze, so every portion carries a similar, estimated dose.
excerpt: A smoky chuck roast that stays plain through the long cook, then gets a measured infused BBQ glaze on each plate, so every portion gets an even, estimated share of the dose.
keyTakeaways: The roast cooks plain. The THC goes into a BBQ glaze brushed on each portion just before serving.
Long heat can cost you THC, and a braise carries fat into the pan juices, so the infusion stays out of the pot.
Total THC in the glaze divided by the number of plates gives the estimated dose per plate.
No smoker? Sear and braise in the oven or a slow cooker. The glaze step stays the same.
body:
Yes, it's a pot roast with pot in it, but this cannabis pot roast keeps the infusion out of the long cook. The smoked chuck roast cooks plain until it's fork-tender. The THC arrives at the end, in an infused BBQ glaze measured onto each plate.

## Where the dose goes

Hours of heat and a pan full of rendered fat would turn the dose per plate into a guess. So the infusion goes into the glaze instead. Add up the THC in the [canna-honey](/blog/canna-honey/) or [cannabutter](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) you stir into the sauce, and split that total across the plates you'll serve. Then mix until the glaze is completely even. New to edibles? Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) covers starting amounts.

## Cannabis pot roast ingredients

A 3 to 4 pound chuck roast takes a rub of kosher salt, pepper, garlic powder and smoked paprika. A shallot, garlic and green onions go into the wrap, and cider vinegar in a spray bottle keeps the bark moist.

For the glaze, stir measured canna-honey into a BBQ sauce you love, or make our [sweet and smoky BBQ sauce](/blog/sweet-and-smokey-bbq-sauce/). Making your infusion from scratch? Browse your nearest High Society store's [online menu](/shop/) for flower and order ahead for curbside pickup.

## Smoker, oven or slow cooker

This infused pot roast recipe works three ways. On a smoker, hold about 250 °F and mist the roast hourly until a dark bark sets. Then wrap it with the aromatics and cook until a probe slides in easily. Indoors, sear the roast and braise it covered at 300 °F for 3 to 4 hours, or give it about 8 hours on low in a slow cooker.

## Glaze each plate at the table

Slice or pull the rested roast and plate it. Spoon the measured glaze over each portion right before serving. Set out plain BBQ sauce too, clearly marked, so a second helping of sauce never means a second dose.

## Leftovers and labels

Refrigerate leftovers within two hours, keeping plain and glazed portions apart. Label the infused ones 'contains THC' with the date and estimated dose. They keep 3 to 4 days; reheat plain meat to 165 °F before glazing. Keep infused food away from children and pets, and if someone eats it by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.a: Not all at once, but it doesn't help. In lab heating studies, THC in cannabis extracts peaked and then fell as heating went on, possibly through evaporation. Heat, air and light can turn some THC into CBN. A braise also melts the fat carrying the THC into the pan juices. A glaze added at the end avoids both problems.

faq.q: How do I keep each plate's dose the same?
faq.a: Measure the glaze, not the meat. Mix the infusion into the warm sauce until it's uniform, then use the same spoon or a small ramekin for every plate, and brush all of it on. Plain sauce on the table covers anyone who wants more flavor without more THC.

faq.q: What internal temperature makes chuck roast tender?
faq.a: Around 195 to 205 °F. Chuck has plenty of connective tissue that needs time in that range to soften, so it slices neatly at the low end and pulls apart at the high end. Trust the probe test as much as the number, then rest a smoked roast at least 30 minutes.

ingredients: 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar in a spray bottle (smoker method)
1 cup BBQ sauce for the glaze, plus plain sauce for the table
Canna-honey, cannabutter or a THC tincture, measured for 8 servings (see the dosing note)
steps: Stir together the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Pat the roast dry and press the rub into every side.
Smoker: hold it near 250 °F. Smoke the roast for about 4 hours, misting it with cider vinegar every hour, until the outside is dark and firm.
Set the roast on a double layer of foil or butcher paper, scatter the shallot, garlic and green onion around it, add a splash of broth and wrap it snugly. Return it to the smoker.
Cook until a probe glides in with almost no resistance, about 195 to 205 °F at the center, roughly 3 more hours. Rest it, still wrapped, for 30 to 60 minutes.

Oven or slow cooker instead: brown the rubbed roast on all sides in a hot Dutch oven, add the aromatics and broth, and cover. Braise at 300 °F for 3 to 4 hours, or cook on low in a slow cooker for about 8 hours, until tender. Rest 20 minutes.
For the glaze, warm the BBQ sauce over low heat, take the pan off the burner, and stir in the measured infusion until completely blended.
Slice or pull the roast and plate 8 equal portions. Spoon or brush the same amount of glaze over each one and serve.
recipe.dosingNote: **Estimate the dose per plate:** total THC in the infusion you stir into the glaze ÷ 8 plates. Example: canna-honey carrying about 40 mg THC in total works out to roughly 5 mg per plate, if the glaze is fully mixed and evenly portioned. A homemade infusion's real strength depends on how potent your starting flower was and on losses during decarboxylation and infusion, so the figure is only an estimate. Start low and wait at least 2 hours before more. Label leftovers, and keep infused food away from children and pets.

sources.label: Wang M. et al. (2016), Decarboxylation study of acidic cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
University of Illinois Extension: Leftovers (food safety)

review.summary: 17 claims checked: 14 ok, 3 overstated (fixed). No wrong legal or High Society claim.

claims.claim: Long heat can cost you THC (takeaway; 'Where the dose goes')
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST), reviewing earlier work: 'Maximum formation of Δ9-THC was observed in ∼5–10 min at 145°C followed by a significant loss at longer times possibly due to evaporation of Δ9-THC'; 'formation of an oxidation product, CBN, was observed at 160°C and 180°C'

claims.claim: FAQ: in lab studies THC in heated extracts peaked and then dropped 'through evaporation and oxidation into CBN'
claims.fix: now 'possibly through evaporation', with a separate sentence that heat, air and light can turn some THC into CBN: the peak-then-loss result Wang reviews names evaporation only as a possibility, and Wang's own vacuum-oven runs found no CBN
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/: 'possibly due to evaporation of Δ9-THC'; 'Δ9-THC itself readily oxidizes to cannabinol (CBN) with oxygen and light during the decarboxylation process'; own result: 'In particular, no CBN (a common oxidation by-product) was observed under the experimental conditions'

claims.claim: A braise melts the fat carrying the THC into the pan juices, so the infusion stays out of the pot
claims.source: reasoning, no figure: a cannabutter or canna-oil infusion holds its THC in the fat, which renders into the braising liquid

claims.claim: Dose per plate = total THC in the glaze ÷ plates; example about 40 mg ÷ 8 = roughly 5 mg, as an estimate
claims.source: arithmetic (40 ÷ 8 = 5); framed as an example, not a fixed figure per spoon, as the brief requires

claims.claim: A homemade infusion's strength depends on the flower's potency and on decarboxylation and infusion losses (dosing note)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/: 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: Smoker near 250 °F, about 4 hours to set the bark, then wrapped about 3 more hours (cook time 7 hours)
claims.source: https://www.smokedbbqsource.com/poor-mans-brisket/ (WebFetch): 'Set your smoker to 250°F.'; 'Total cook time: 5–8 hours for most 3–5 lb chuck roasts, plus rest'

claims.claim: Chuck turns tender around 195 to 205 °F at the center; slices at the low end, pulls at the high end; trust the probe test
claims.source: https://www.smokedbbqsource.com/poor-mans-brisket/: 'until it reaches an internal temperature of 195-205°F or when it is probe tender'; 'Finish cooking until probe tender, usually 200–210°F internal'

claims.claim: FAQ: rest the roast at least 30 minutes (the oven step says rest 20 minutes)
claims.fix: FAQ now says 'rest a smoked roast at least 30 minutes', matching the smoker step (30 to 60 minutes) and leaving the braise at 20

claims.claim: Oven: sear, then braise covered at 300 °F for 3 to 4 hours (3 to 4 lb roast)
claims.source: https://www.tastingtable.com/2187033/ideal-oven-temperature-tender-chuck-roast/ (WebFetch): 'an oven set at 300 degrees Fahrenheit'; 'One hour per pound of chuck will yield a tender, juicy roast'

claims.claim: Slow cooker: about 8 hours on low
claims.source: https://agriculture.vermont.gov/slow-cooker-pot-roast (WebFetch): '3 lb chuck roast'; 'Cook on low for 8 hours, or high for 4-5 hours.'

claims.claim: Refrigerate leftovers within two hours; they keep 3 to 4 days; reheat plain meat to 165 °F
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers (WebFetch): 'Leftover food should be refrigerated or frozen within two hours of serving.'; 'Use refrigerated leftover food within 3-4 days'; 'reheat to a minimum of 165 F'

claims.claim: If someone eats it by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Start low and wait at least 2 hours before more
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12648025/ (Grotenhermen 2003, abstract via E-utilities): oral effects 'set in with a delay of 30-90 minutes, reach their maximum after 2-3 hours'

claims.claim: Label infused leftovers and keep infused food away from children and pets
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'Infants or young children who unintentionally ingest cannabis are more likely to require hospital admission'

claims.claim: High Society: browse your nearest store's online menu for flower and order ahead for curbside pickup
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering ('Online order for pickup: browse the store menu online ... ask for curbside and get a text when ready'), services.curbside ('offered at every store'), services.productCategories (flower); no strain or product named as stocked

claims.claim: Meta description 'a dose you can count'; excerpt 'every portion has a known dose'
claims.fix: now 'a similar, estimated dose' and 'an even, estimated share of the dose', matching the dosing note, which calls a homemade figure an estimate

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Wang 2016 re-read in full through the Europe PMC REST API: its 145 °C peak-then-loss figure is a review of earlier work, not Wang's own result, so the FAQ now keeps the mechanism tentative. Cooking times and temperatures checked against a BBQ reference, Tasting Table and a Vermont Agency of Agriculture recipe; food-safety figures against Illinois Extension; onset and Poison Control against the CDC FAQ. Sources list kept (all three open, https, and support the text as now worded). No legal claims. High Society: one mention (online menu, order ahead, curbside), all in hs-facts; no prices, phone, hours, app or stocked product. Writer's notes: Dose moved to a finishing glaze per the brief angle. No brand, no named staff, no fixed mg as fact (example only). High Society mentioned once (online menu for flower, curbside pickup).
writerClaims: THC peaks then falls with longer/hotter heating, partly by oxidation to CBN: Wang 2016 full text ("Maximum formation of Δ9-THC was observed in ∼5–10 min at 145°C followed by a significant loss at longer times"; "Δ9-THC itself readily oxidizes to cannabinol (CBN)").
Edible effects can take up to 2 hours; Poison Control 1-800-222-1222: CDC cannabis FAQ.
